24 THE SAVOY MALE AND FEMALE COLLEGE

of the school, for the year 1887-1888, the coverage of the curriculum is indicated to be:

Orthography
First, Second, Third and Fourth Readers
Primary and Rudimentary Arithmetic
Primary History of the United States

As, according to the memory of students of the time, the beginner had to spell for over a year using the "Blue-Back" Speller, and this primary curriculum was allowing a year for each of the McGuffey's Readers—the standard pace-setters of the time—was three years in practice.

The Preparatory Department seems likely to have required another three years, by one year's work for each; so that the requirements for a four-year primary curriculum required another three years of work to complete before the entrance into the Collegiate Department:

Practical Arithmetic
Practical Grammar
Good Morals and Gentle Manners
Map Drawing
Fifth and Sixth Readers
History of the United States
Physical Geography

As the subjects were taken verbatim from the titles of the books, it is evident that many of them furnished a few class and no text books. But the catalog for 1885, with many of these courses, was a great deal of a great course. We are going to find that many of the course books were not always the best.
